name: design-canvas
description: A live Claude Design canvas in a pane - the real pan/zoom canvas editor from Claude Code's bundled `design` skill, seeded from `.dc.html` artboard files in a folder on disk and re-seeded automatically whenever one of them changes. Reach for it whenever the work is VISUAL and you are drafting it as files: a UI mockup or screen flow, a landing page, a poster/flyer/one-pager, a report laid out as artboards. Mount it once and the user WATCHES the layout change as you write it instead of reading you describe it, and can pin comments on the artboards. It is not a viewer for someone else's work: it only ever shows canvases seeded from the user's OWN local working files, never an Artifact URL and never a published canvas. READ-ONLY on those files - the service reads `dir` and never creates, modifies or deletes anything under it, and there is no WYSIWYG Save: the editor boots read-only here (this pack serves it no capability object), so the pipeline is ONE-WAY - `.dc.html` files to canvas - and a design is changed by editing those files and letting the service re-seed. Nothing can travel back the other way, by construction. Do not offer `--extract` as a round trip; it is the helper's way back into files from a canvas edited SOMEWHERE ELSE (a published Artifact someone saved), and it is the user's command, never this pack's. For real click-to-edit-and-Save, hand off to a published Artifact via the bundled `design` skill instead. SERVICE-BACKED, so it is inert until the user runs `claude-web-chat trust design-canvas` in their TERMINAL: say that command in chat in the same breath as mounting the pane, because the pane can only name it and cannot grant it. Consent is keyed on (project root, service.js contents, params), so changing `dir`, `title`, `isolate` or `watch` asks again - `routing` does not, being shell-read - and the service runs only while its pane is on the ACTIVE node with a browser watching (navigate away and it stops, navigate back and it respawns). It also needs Claude Design to exist on this machine: the editor payload is materialised into a temp directory the first time the bundled `design` skill runs in a session, so if it never has, the pane renders state `no-payload` and the one fix is to run `/design` once in Claude Code. Writes `dsn_canvas` - `{seq, ok, state, payload_component, title, artboards, seeded_at, bytes, upstream, error, hint}`, where `state` is one of ready | seeding | no-payload | bad-dir | seed-failed | live-store, and every failure carries human prose in `error` plus the ONE action that fixes it in `hint` (a `seed-failed` carries the seeding helper's stderr verbatim, which is written to be read) - and `dsn_files` `{seq, dir, files:[{name, bytes, mtime}], has_canvas_json}`, which is the cheapest way to see what is actually on disk without a second read. Reads the CONTROL key `dsn_ctl {seq, op}` - `op` `reseed` (re-run the helper against the current files, always safe) or `rescan` (re-read the directory listing only) - which the service watches over SSE: a user panning, zooming or clicking NEVER wakes Claude. You may drive it yourself, but `set_store` needs its patch wrapper - `set_store({patch:{dsn_ctl:{seq:Date.now(), op:'reseed'}}})` - a bare `set_store({dsn_ctl:...})` is a silent no-op that still returns ok, and `seq` must strictly increase or the write is ignored. ONE declared signal, `dsn_ask {seq, note, artboard}`, written only when the user hits Ask Claude: declare it TOP-LEVEL on use_component (`signals:[{key:'dsn_ask', wake:'queue'}]`) while `routing:'none'` goes INSIDE `params`. That asymmetry is the easiest thing here to get wrong - use_component reads `signals` only at the top level and `routing` only inside params, and each is dropped in silence in the wrong place. `routing:'none'` does not suppress the signal; the queue classifier tests declared keys before the routing opt-out. Params: `dir` and `title` are required, `title` being CONTENT-named because the seeding helper hard-refuses a title that names the tool instead of the design; `isolate:true` sandboxes the frame to an opaque origin and TURNS PINS OFF; `watch:false` stops the 250 ms-debounced re-seed. Two degraded contexts it handles rather than blanking: node previews and glance cards get a static placeholder (their CSP is `default-src 'none'`, so both the frame and the fetch are dead) and so do frozen exports (the pane's fetch runs against no server) - the right export for a canvas is the seeded `.html` itself, which is already self-contained and interactive. It also needs a SECURE CONTEXT: fine on localhost, 127.0.0.1 and https, but over plain http to a LAN IP or an mDNS name the canvas hangs on a permanent spinner, so the pane warns before mounting the frame. Finally, the service writes a runtime-only carrier component into this project to hand the 2.4 MB editor to the pane. Its name is `design-canvas-payload-<8 hex>` - per MOUNT, not fixed, so two design-canvas panes on one node cannot clobber each other's payload; never hardcode it, read `dsn_canvas.payload_component` for the real one. It shows up in list_components, the drawer and the command palette. NEVER mount it: one accidental mount snapshots 2.4 MB into every committed graph node, forever.

dir.title: Folder holding the artboard files - an absolute path
dir.description: ABSOLUTE path to the working directory whose `.dc.html` artboards make up this canvas. It must already contain at least one `<Name>.dc.html`; a missing, unreadable or artboard-less folder renders state `bad-dir` naming the path and what was expected, never a silent fallback. `canvas.json` beside them is optional and supplies the layout (per-artboard x/y/w/h, sticky notes, pages, launch); without it the artboards lay out in a row and `dsn_canvas.artboards` reports null geometry. Images (.png .jpg .jpeg .gif .webp .avif .bmp .svg) in the folder are picked up automatically and stored inside the canvas, so keep each one small - the editor drops any file entry over 2 MiB at load. The path is FENCED inside the project: one that resolves outside it is refused as `bad-dir` rather than read. Nothing here is ever written to - the service only reads. Changing this re-asks the `claude-web-chat trust design-canvas` approval, which is correct, because it widens what the service can read.

title.title: What this design is called - name it from the content, not from the tool
title.description: The canvas's own title. It lands in the page title and in the seeded state block, and a slug of it names the seeded file. The seeding helper enforces this and exits 1 on a bad value, which surfaces as state `seed-failed` with its stderr verbatim, so get it right at spawn time: it is REFUSED if it is empty, over 120 characters, contains a less-than, greater-than, ampersand, double-quote, backslash or control character (apostrophes are fine), or is one of the generic names that describe the tool rather than the design - design, canvas, design canvas, new design, untitled, appifact, new appifact, artifact - compared case-insensitively after trimming. Name it the way the user would refer to it.

isolate.title: Sandbox the canvas frame - safer, but turns pins off completely
isolate.description: Leave this off for the normal case, which is the only case this component supports: artboards you or the user authored in `dir`. Turning it on sandboxes the canvas frame to an opaque origin, so nothing inside it can reach the local daemon - the right stance for any content you would not vouch for. The cost is total: an opaque-origin frame cannot be read from, so no anchors can be projected and pins are unavailable, not merely degraded. Changing this re-asks the `claude-web-chat trust design-canvas` approval.

watch.title: Re-seed automatically when a file in the folder changes
watch.description: On by default, and it is what makes the pane worth mounting: the service watches `dir` for changes to `*.dc.html`, `canvas.json` and images, debounces them for 250 ms, re-runs the seeding helper and bumps `dsn_canvas.seq` - so the canvas keeps up with the files you write, with no turn of yours involved. Turn it off for a frozen snapshot, or when a build process rewrites the folder in a way that would thrash the re-seed. Either way you can still force one at any time by writing the control key: `set_store({patch:{dsn_ctl:{seq:Date.now(), op:'reseed'}}})`. Changing this re-asks the `claude-web-chat trust design-canvas` approval.

routing.title: Activity routing - leave this as none
routing.description: `none` is the only valid value. Without it every pan, zoom and selection on the canvas coalesces into per-mount activity items that reach the queue on the user's next Push - pure noise, because this pane has a deliberate wake of its own in the `dsn_ask` signal, and it does not suppress that signal (declared keys are classified before the routing opt-out). This key is read by the web-chat shell rather than by the pane, and it is stripped before the service's trust fingerprint, so it never re-asks for approval. When you mount this component yourself, note the asymmetry: `routing` goes INSIDE `params`, while `signals:[{key:'dsn_ask', wake:'queue'}]` goes at the TOP LEVEL of the use_component call.
